anomalies.title: Abnormal coolant pressure deviation
anomalies.description: Coolant pressure deviated significantly from its established baseline during the analysed incident window.

possible_causes.cause: Abnormal operating condition or resource contention

recommendations.action: Inspect the coolant circuit, associated components, and pressure-control mechanism.
Compare the affected incident window against previous normal operating traces.

anomalies.title: Repeated equipment alarm activity
anomalies.description: Multiple alarm state transitions occurred within the same incident period and overlap temporally with the primary signal deviation.

possible_causes.cause: Secondary response to abnormal equipment operating conditions

recommendations.action: Correlate the alarm transitions with coolant and hydraulic signal changes.

insights.summary: The analysed equipment experienced a significant increase in anomalous behaviour during the incident window, with coolant pressure deviation temporally associated with repeated alarm activity.

root_cause_hypotheses.description: The coolant subsystem is the leading root-cause hypothesis because its pressure signal shows a significant deviation from baseline and occurs during the primary anomaly window.
The observed alarm cluster may represent a downstream consequence of the abnormal coolant operating condition rather than an independent initiating fault.

recommendations.action: Inspect the coolant subsystem and pressure-control components before returning the equipment to normal operation.
Review the temporal relationship between coolant pressure, hydraulic pressure, and alarm transitions.
